text:
Explain the two stages clearly. Deidentified NHANES data and other CDC public health sources supported model development and testing. The standalone model project used participant level splits and held out evaluation. Once the team saw that the models could produce meaningful experimental results, fictional sample profiles were used to demonstrate how compatible fields and outputs might appear inside WellPath. The research project does not connect to the application or its database.

The cycle tracker demonstrates a transparent estimation concept. Logged cycle start dates produce cycle lengths. Recent lengths are averaged to estimate the next cycle start, and variability in the history informs the confidence range. The example screen uses sample history and should not be presented as a validated prediction tool.

text:
The standalone research project compares multiple model types with participant level data splits. The methodology includes training, validation, and held out testing for the multi condition panel, with preprocessing contained inside the model pipeline. ROC curves summarize how well models separate predefined categories in the research dataset. Good separation in one dataset does not prove diagnosis, clinical safety, transportability, fairness, or benefit.

text:
State the boundaries directly. Sample profiles are fictional. The models are exploratory research models and are not clinically validated. Associations do not establish causes, and classification does not establish a diagnosis. A real product would require external and prospective validation, clinical utility studies, privacy and security safeguards, subgroup fairness evaluation, deployment monitoring, and relevant regulatory review.
